answer: The network can throttle new identities by trade allowance: an identity begins copper-poor, allowed only micro transfers, and its cap grows only through epochs of clean, peer-attested history. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes finds every one stuck at micro volume, while honest agents keep their earnings because the onyx-hard ledger of past honesty cannot be faked. A fake cannot rush maturity; the zephyr-fast money it chases moves too slowly through a copper-poor identity to ever be worth the effort.
